minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard Mass Ave main funding options and Hickory Hills pilot update; no Zoom decision made.
minutes.summary: The commissioners reviewed the Hickory Hills PFAS pilot study (notice of intent filed, hearing in two weeks), financing options for the Massachusetts Avenue water main, the Lancaster Ave pump test, and a request to Selectmen for ARPA funds. A resident asked the district to offer Zoom; commissioners were mostly opposed and agreed only to look into it. The 110 Bird Street special-meeting request was discussed, awaiting a proper request from the applicant. Minutes of May 10 were moved; the outcome is not audible.

public_comment.topic: Asked to attend and speak in favor of the ARPA education campaign on the 6th, asked for updates on 110 Bird Street, and asked the district to offer Zoom for meetings.

budget_items.what_was_said: The financial advisor offered three hypothetical bond terms after temporary borrowing; the board will choose after temporary borrowing bids.
Two earlier separate projects have money that could be moved over; the rest would come out of the budget or a separate bill line item.
Commissioners compared per-taker quarterly charges for a 20-year loan against a shorter term, and discussed splitting costs with the budget.
A dual band radio was priced against a VHF one; commissioners favored staying on VHF.
Bidding law needs only three quotes at this level; cleaning waits until after November.
The district asked the town for ARPA funds for a three-phase PFAS education, master plan and pilot; town discussed other allocations.

decisions.decision: Commissioners will meet with Selectmen on the 6th to give a breakdown of the ARPA request, and will post it as a district meeting.
Commissioners agreed to look into the Zoom option but made no commitment.
Ask district attorneys about the timeline for calling a special meeting on the 110 Bird Street request.
Prepare scenario-based customer impact options for the water main funding to get public feedback.

what_happened.line: Commissioners reviewed financing options for the Massachusetts Avenue water main and will prepare scenario-based customer impact options to take to the public.
The financial advisor offered three hypothetical bond terms; the board will choose after temporary borrowing bids come in.
Commissioners will meet with Selectmen on the 6th to explain the district's ARPA request for a three-phase PFAS education, master plan and pilot.
Commissioners agreed only to look into offering Zoom after a resident asked, and made no commitment.
The 110 Bird Street special-meeting request awaits a proper request from the applicant; district attorneys will be asked about the timeline.

why_it_matters: How the Massachusetts Avenue main is paid for (bond term, existing project funds, the budget or a separate bill line) decides what customers see on their quarterly water bill.
The ARPA request to the town is a possible outside source for the PFAS work, and the district has asked residents to attend and speak for it at the Selectmen's meeting.
Remote access to commissioners' meetings stays unsettled, so residents who cannot attend in person have no confirmed way to take part.
